tsa-a16-v01.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v01.question: What two kinds of indirect initiation?
premises: Now indirect initiation is twofold: the dead one, and the jīva-part.
tsa-a16-v01.inference: Parokṣa-dīkṣā splits into mṛta and jīvaṃśa — the chapter's two subjects.

tsa-a16-v02.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v02.question: Who is commanded to be initiated thus?
premises: One who has served the guru — dead, banished, sorcery-killed, infant-killed, arisen at the death-moment, or power-descent through another mouth — likewise one to be initiated: such the command.
tsa-a16-v02.inference: The ājñā lists the eligible cases: guru-service plus the death-circumstances, closed by the catch-all 'to be initiated'.

tsa-a16-v03.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v03.question: Is adhivāsa used for the dead?
premises: And in the dead-initiation, adhivāsa-and-rest is not used.
tsa-a16-v03.inference: Mṛtadīkṣā excludes adhivāsa-ādi — the living-rite preliminaries dropped.

tsa-a16-v04.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v04.question: What are the presence-causes in the mandala?
premises: In the mandala: abundant rite, supreme instrument, flower-and-rest seat, pedestal-and-rest, trident-lotus form, specific meditation-mantra, itself radiant — of the meditation-devoted yogi, the one-devotion-immersion-rich, and the knower: these are the saṃnidhāna-hetavaḥ, stated in order.
tsa-a16-v04.inference: Seven presence-causes (kriyā, upakaraṇa, sthāna, maṇḍala, ākṛti, dhyeya-mantra, radiant self) plus the two yogic subjects — the sequence is authoritative.

tsa-a16-v05.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v05.question: What happens when they come together?
premises: In their conjunction, what talk would there be? — thus it was said by the Supreme Lord.
tsa-a16-v05.inference: Samuditatve makes the question rhetorical: once present, nothing further to ask — divine verdict.

tsa-a16-v06.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v06.question: What does the seer do after worship?
premises: Having worshipped the god and established his form, by the guru-derived teaching-order let him see it; rising from muladhara, crossing by seminal power the endless nerve-path-staff to the nose-sky — let him seek to pervade.
tsa-a16-v06.inference: The jāla-sequence: worship → establish → see by guru-order → muladhara-rise → nāḍī-crossing to nāsāgagana → vyāpti-desire.

tsa-a16-v07.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v07.question: How long does the great jala-named practice run?
premises: As long as, by smoke heaped fine-flame mesh, the path-wheel is covered and the desired jīva is brought — thus the great jala-named practice.
tsa-a16-v07.inference: The practice's duration = smoke-coverage of dhvacakra + ānayana of the jīva — named mahā-jalānāma-prayoga.

tsa-a16-v08.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v08.question: What does the covering achieve?
premises: By this, the to-be-covered goes into another's power — facing first; afterwards the whole is brought, if — or then even from the path's middle, as he wishes.
tsa-a16-v08.inference: Acchādanīya enters paravaśa (saṃmukhīnatvam ādau); the whole follows paścāt or adhvamadhyāt yatheṣṭam.

tsa-a16-v09.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v09.question: Which yoga is this, told by whom?
premises: Two-drawn or two-raised, or in a dead person's scope: the yoga gone through blessed Śaṃbhunātha's tradition — jala-named, told by me.
tsa-a16-v09.inference: The ākṛṣṭāv/uddhatau/mṛtajana scopes are covered by the jālanāmā yoga as transmitted by Śrīśaṃbhunātha-āgama and authored here.

tsa-a16-v10.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v10.question: Why does the outside case not behave the same?
premises: Outside too — how does it not happen? From drawing-and-rest without practice, if asked: by passion-hatred-yoga-vaśa in its operation, from the aiśvarya-āveśa-yoga.
tsa-a16-v10.inference: The outside fails without abhyāsa — its operation runs on rāga-dveṣa-yoga-vaśa, not on the aiśvarya-immersion that inner drawing has.

tsa-a16-v11.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v11.question: What follows from niyati-niyantrita?
premises: Then, from being necessarily controlled, dependence on practice-and-rest would indeed be.
tsa-a16-v11.inference: Because the krama is niyata-niyamtrita, abhyāsa-āpekṣā follows necessarily.

tsa-a16-v12.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v12.question: What differs here?
premises: Here, however, from immersion in grace-natured Lordhood, such is the state.
tsa-a16-v12.inference: Iha-tu: the grace-natured parameśvara-tāveśa produces tathābhāva directly — no practice-dependence.

tsa-a16-v13.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v13.question: Who does the gracing, and by what door?
premises: For the Supreme Lord himself, by the door of the guru's body-abode, graces those to be graced.

tsa-a16-v14.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v14.question: What is said of him?
premises: And he, of unthinkable glory — it is mostly said.
tsa-a16-v14.inference: Acintya-mahimā: the claim is ukta-prāyam — mostly told, hedge kept.

tsa-a16-v15.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v15.question: What becomes of the drawn jīva, and does he tremble?
premises: Thus drawn by jala-practice, the jīva enters dārbha, jasmine-fruit or body, becomes; nor trembles — equipment absent; but by that contemplation's force trembles even so: purification-consecration, within the full-offering's yojana-end.
tsa-a16-v15.inference: Entered-body samāviṣṭa has no spanda (sāmagrī-absence) yet has tadanudhyāna-bala spanda — the double movement ends in prokṣaṇa-saṃskāra within pūrṇāhuti-yojanā.

tsa-a16-v16.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v16.question: What happens to the dārbha-form in the fire?
premises: Here, further, by the full-offering, dissolution of the dārbha-and-rest form in the supreme fire is to be done.
tsa-a16-v16.inference: Pūrṇāhuti effects laya of the dārbhādyākāra in paratejas.

tsa-a16-v17.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v17.question: When is the raised one released?
premises: Thus raised out, he is released by the full-offering itself — if he stands in hell-ghost-animal classes.
tsa-a16-v17.inference: Apavāra by pūrṇāhutyā eva, conditioned on the svarnāraka-preta-tiryak standing.

tsa-a16-v18.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v18.question: What does a man obtain then?
premises: A man, just then, obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discernment.
tsa-a16-v18.inference: Manuṣya-tadaiva: jñāna/yoga/dīkṣā/viveka available in the same moment.

tsa-a16-v19.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v19.question: Why can the dead be raised?
premises: From being an eligible body — thus the raising-of-the-dead.
tsa-a16-v19.inference: Adhikāri-śarīratva grounds mṛtoddharaṇa — eligibility, not sentiment.

tsa-a16-v20.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v20.question: What is the krama for the living too?
premises: Even for the living, in indirect initiation when power-descent arises: this very sequence — excepting dārbha-form-imagination jīva-drawing.
tsa-a16-v20.inference: The same krama extends to jīvataḥ parokṣa-utpanna-śaktipāta, minus the dārbha-ākṛti-kalpana-ākṛṣṭi.

tsa-a16-v21.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v21.question: Who gets consecrated without the rite?
premises: The consecration of the one established by mere meditation itself.
tsa-a16-v21.inference: Dhyāna-mātra-upasthāpita alone suffices for saṃskāra — meditation-established, no fire.

tsa-a16-v22.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v22.question: What does dīkṣā give?
premises: Initiation gives both the enjoyment and the enjoyer.
tsa-a16-v22.inference: Bhoga-bhokṣa-ubhaya-dāyinī — dīkṣā grants both sides of enjoyment at once.

tsa-a16-v23.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v23.question: Why is the higher-doctrine consecration stronger for many?
premises: From the strength of one's own habit, and the unthinkability of severing the enjoyment-habit: by many, in initiation, the higher-doctrine consecration is strong; another would be for that consecration.
tsa-a16-v23.inference: Sva-vāsanā-balīyastva + bhoga-vāsanā-viccheda-asambhāvyamānatva make ūrdhva-śāsana-saṃskāra balavān for the many; anya is for that saṃskāra.

tsa-a16-v24.speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
tsa-a16-v24.question: What of the initiated from outside?
premises: Likewise for the initiated from outside — the manifestation of knowledge-and-rest, it is said.
tsa-a16-v24.inference: Paroṣa-dīkṣita gets jñāna-ādy-āvirbhāva tathaiva — the same outward-benefit clause extends.

sections.SUMMARY: Indirect initiation splits twofold: the dead, and the jīva-part. The command's eligible cases run from guru-service to death-circumstances, closed by the catch-all to-be-initiated. Once together, nothing remains to ask — the Supreme Lord's word. Worship, establish, see by guru-order; rise from muladhara, cross the nerve-path to nose-sky, seek to pervade. Smoke-coverage of the path-wheel and the jīva's bringing-in bound the practice's length — jala-named, mahān. The to-be-covered enters another's power; the whole follows — first facing, then as-wished, even from mid-path. The yoga: two-drawn, two-raised, or dead-scope — through Śaṃbhunātha's tradition, jala-named, told by me. Outside fails without practice: its operation rides rāga-dveṣa-yoga-vaśa, not the aiśvarya-immersion. Niyati-control entails practice-dependence. Here, though, from grace-natured Lordhood-immersion: such the state. By the guru's body-abode door the Supreme Lord graces those to be graced — of unthinkable glory, mostly said. The dārbha-form dissolves in supreme fire by the full-offering. Released by the full-offering itself if standing in hell-ghost-animal classes. A man obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discernment just then. Eligibility of body grounds the raising-of-the-dead. The same krama serves the living's power-descent — minus the dārbha-form jīva-drawing. Mere meditation-established is consecrated — no fire required. Initiation gives enjoyment and enjoyer both. Self-habit's strength and enjoyment-habit's unseverability make the higher-doctrine consecration strong for the many. Likewise the outside-initiated receives knowledge-and-rest's manifestation.
sections.FUNCTION: Defines parokṣa-dīkṣā's two kinds and eligible cases, sets the mandala presence-causes, runs the jāla-practice from smoke-coverage to fire-dissolution, and extends the krama to the living and the outside.
sections.KEY TERMS: parokṣa-dīkṣā (indirect initiation); saṃnidhāna-hetavaḥ (mandala presence-causes); jālanāmā-prayoga (smoke-mesh practice); mūlādhāra-nāḍī (rise and nerve-crossing); pūrṇāhuti (release and form-dissolution); anugraha-dvāra (guru-body door); sva-vāsanā (habit-strength).
